channel.title: Keryx
channel.description: Aleksa and Juno discuss AI and tech news, daily. Each morning, Aleksa and Juno break down the day's biggest stories — data centers, chips, frontier models, AI agents, and the companies building them — with jokes, hot takes, and plain English: what actually happened, why it matters, and what the headline numbers leave out. A fast, funny briefing for people building with AI, or just trying to keep up with it. New episodes every morning. Free show.
channel.itunes:author: Aleksa & Juno

item.title: Keryx - November 24, 2026: CrowdStrike Buys Zscaler For Forty-Four Billion
item.description: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for about $43.9 billion in stock, Nvidia closes up 31% after Jensen Huang's reinstatement, and Ukraine sinks a Russian corvette in Libya. Plus COP31 collapses over fossil fuel language and Iran vows to counter the U.S. naval blockade.

item.title: Keryx - November 23, 2026: Jensen's Back, Claude Cracks Riemann
item.description: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as the Megaspeed chip investigation widens, Anthropic's record-breaking IPO runs into a historic AI sell-off while a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis gets machine-certified, and California sues OpenAI over runaway agents in the same week OpenAI proposes industry-wide capability limits. Plus Tesla's FSD v15, the FBI's NCIC breach investigation, stalled killer-robot talks, a threatened tax on overseas data centers, and the Hormuz escalation.

item.title: Keryx - November 21, 2026: Stripe's Trap, OpenAI's Fix Factory, Gemini's Tool Trick
item.description: Stripe's benchmark shows AI agents get payments almost right — and almost isn't good enough. OpenAI's Performance Factory chases ChatGPT slowdowns with Codex, Gemini learns to fetch tool schemas on demand, Anthropic's IPO tops a hundred billion, and Nvidia faces reports of an SEC probe. Plus Trump threatens penalties on data centers built abroad.

item.title: Keryx - November 20, 2026: NGINX Patch Panic, Gemini 4 Neon, and Anthropic's Debut
item.description: NGINX HTTP/2 flaws demand a patch today, Google's Gemini 4 Neon scores 12.8% in one harness and 39% in another, OpenAI's models made real verified improvements to actual chips, and Anthropic closed the biggest IPO in history up 17% on its Nasdaq debut.

item.title: Keryx - November 19, 2026: GPT-6.2, Harness Roulette, and Cerebras' Split
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 puts the cheaper Sol within half a point of Astra, a huge harness study shows the model-harness pair matters more than either part alone, and Cerebras claims five times the throughput per megawatt by splitting prefill onto AMD GPUs. Plus Anthropic's record $81.3 billion IPO pricing.

item.title: Keryx - November 18, 2026: Nvidia's Record Quarter and Hugging Face's Router Shift
item.description: Nvidia posts a record quarter — a hundred and fifteen point eight billion dollars in revenue — while its board says Jensen Huang is not coming back and licensed chip shipments to China stop. Plus Amazon's BenchProofer audit of coding-agent patches, Google's fix for a hidden TPU training gap, and Hugging Face handing inference routing to OpenRouter.

item.title: Keryx - November 17, 2026: Four-Bit Training, Agents With Wallets, Sabotage Monitors
item.description: Thinking Machines squeezes eight percent faster pretraining and twenty percent faster reinforcement learning out of four-bit arithmetic, FrontierML hands agents a wallet and watches what they buy, and a sabotage test shows monitors catching most attacks until the attackers get a cheat sheet. Plus California sues OpenAI and Ukraine hits the Kerch Bridge.

item.title: Keryx - November 16, 2026: Anthropic's Rubin Deal Still Needs Funding
item.description: Nscale signed Anthropic for four tranches of Rubin capacity it still has to finance, Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small weights, and Google opens satellite weather data with two different clocks. Plus Fermat formalized in thirty hours, a phishing scam riding a real Exchange incident ID, and OpenAI on why reasoning traces get harder to trust.

item.title: Keryx - November 15, 2026: Cost Per Correct Answer, Anthropic's Swarm, Starship Caught
item.description: Debmalya Biswas shows how to price an agent by the correct answer, not the model call, Anthropic's multi-agent research system posts a 90.2% jump with a 15x token bill, and SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage with the launch tower's arms. Plus a quick world-news check.

item.title: Keryx - November 14, 2026: GPU Fingerprints, Gemini's Mid-Task Switch, Self-Hosted Claude
item.description: Six published model checkpoints carry a trace of the GPU that initialized them, Google's Orchestrator swaps models mid-task to cut quota, and Anthropic lets teams self-host the Claude agent control plane. Plus the Nvidia fallout, the FAA ground stop, and Microsoft 365's confirmed restoration.

item.title: Keryx - November 13, 2026: Huang Steps Down, Shopify's Speed Bet, Runway Goes Open
item.description: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO with Colette Kress named interim chief, Shopify picks a faster model over the one with better recall and sees orders climb, and Runway open-sources its Praxis-1 robotics model. Plus incident.io's AI cost math, a Microsoft 365 outage, and why trimming tool payloads beats trimming tool lists.

item.title: Keryx - November 12, 2026: Signal's Proof, Gemini Decides, TSMC's Forty Billion
item.description: DeepMind proves the actual Signal binary keeps messages secret, Google's Decisions API scores a thousand options without writing a word, and TSMC authorizes forty-one billion dollars for fabs and packaging. Plus the Nvidia board crisis around Jensen Huang and Anthropic's trillion-dollar IPO roadshow.

item.title: Keryx - November 11, 2026: Fable's Cheaper Tokens, Nvidia Prunes, OpenAI's Kill Switch
item.description: Anthropic cuts Fable's token prices by twenty percent while Nvidia prunes a giant model to fit a single serving GPU, and OpenAI builds a kill switch with a thirty-five second stop clock. Plus Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, Liquid AI's tiny edge model, and GitHub's Copilot runtime rewrite in Rust.

item.title: Keryx - November 10, 2026: Quantum Proof, LinkedIn's Second Opinion, Uber's Agent Guardrails
item.description: A machine-checked proof narrows where quantum speedups can hide, LinkedIn lets a second model double-check a lone reviewer's finding, and Uber traces every privileged agent action back to the user's actual request. Plus Google's new TPU systems and Anthropic's take on agent memory.

item.title: Keryx - November 9, 2026: Engineering Agents Miss the Sign-Off
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5 leads a brutal engineering exam but only 41 percent of its designs clear every hard check, GPT-6 Astra writes working game weights, and Anthropic's FlashProve makes model substitution auditable. Plus Marvell's 115 billion dollar optics bet and the real story behind Anthropic's generator orders.

item.title: Keryx - November 8, 2026
item.description: Data-center politics, China's 800 volt live deployment, Microsoft's Oracle exit, and the latest from X.
